kept.heading: GLM-5.4 (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, its first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer. The design reuses a shared block of layers to reason more deeply without adding parameters. Z.ai says it reaches intelligence comparable to 2T to 3T parameter models, and it is available now on the GLM Coding Plan.

kept.heading: CLAUDE SHIP (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Claude Ship is a set of Anthropic agents that help get GitHub pull requests ready to merge. Code Review flags issues, PR Steward pushes fixes, and Claude Approvals checks changes against a team's approval policy.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING NATURAL VOICE (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Natural Voice enables voice agents to securely process payments during calls, eliminating the need for out-of-band transfers and reducing customer drop-off. By handling PCI compliance, it allows businesses to offer seamless payment experiences without additional compliance burdens. This innovation benefits industries like restaurants, healthcare, and auto services by integrating payment processing directly into voice interactions, enhancing conversion rates and operational efficiency.

kept.heading: SUPERCHARGING TRANSFORMER RESIDUAL CONNECTIONS (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google's DeepCrossAttention (DCA) enhances transformer residual connections by allowing each layer to dynamically select and route features from preceding layers, reducing information dilution and parameter count by 30-40%. Unlike traditional residual connections, DCA uses dynamic routing and depth-wise cross-attention mechanisms to achieve faster convergence and better quality with minimal parameter increase. Tested on large datasets like C4 and LM1B, DCA improves training efficiency and perplexity compared to standard models, proving a shift towards dynamic residual routing for scalable LLMs.

kept.heading: I USED TO ORCHESTRATE AGENTS. NOW I ORCHESTRATE ORCHESTRATORS (24 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: MindRoom significantly enhances AI-driven coding by integrating multiple models in one room, efficiently managing up to forty concurrent sessions with seamless context switching. This approach, which utilizes minimal sub-agents, boosts productivity by maintaining low token overhead and offering a compact, card-based interface that organizes tasks by status.

kept.heading: RECURSIVE SELF-EDITING: LLMS PROGRAM THEIR OWN WEIGHT EDITS FOR SELF-IMPROVEMENT (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Today's language models improve themselves through data, training recipes, or scaffolds. Whenever their weights change, gradient descent writes the update, not the model. SELFWRITE lets the model write its own weights. Each generation, the current model studies its own reasoning on fresh training problems, inspects its own weights and activations in a persistent Python session, and writes a program that constructs a low-rank weight edit for itself from white-box primitives. It can raise gate accuracy and accuracy on a held-out test split that the loop never sees without a single gradient step.

kept.heading: OPENAI AND CISCO INTRODUCE SHIRUDO (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Shirudo is an open-source runtime from OpenAI and Cisco that protects running Linux systems while teams roll out patches. It lets teams deploy temporary shields that block exploits without restarting the service.

kept.heading: FASTER QUANTUM ALGORITHMS WITH AGENTS AND FORMAL VERIFICATION (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google DeepMind used teams of Gemini 4 agents to find cheaper versions of known quantum algorithms, with each result proven correct in the Lean theorem prover. One circuit for fusion energy research cut its computing cost by 11.8x.

kept.heading: BECOME A FOUNDING MEMBER OF TLDR'S AI COMMUNITY (2 MINUTE FORM)
kept.blurb: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join [20].

kept.heading: AMAZON SNAPS UP DECART'S AI OPTIMIZATION TECH FOR $7.5B AS IT PREPARES TO SELL TRAINIUM CHIPS (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Amazon has acquired the technology behind the Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), as well as Decart's founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, for $7.5 billion. Decart has made a name for itself by building interactive real-time models and AI video-generation tools. Its DOS software helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google's hardware. More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.

kept.heading: NVIDIA BOARD REINSTATES JENSEN HUANG AS PRESIDENT, CEO, AND BOARD DIRECTOR (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and Board Director following unanimous Board approval and US government input confirming no national security risk. A committee of independent directors is investigating claims of Huang being targeted by foreign intelligence and will proceed with legal counsel's support. NVIDIA is forming a National Security and Export Control Committee and will appoint a Chief Compliance Officer to enhance oversight.

kept.heading: RL INFRASTRUCTURE AT MICROSOFT AI (15 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Rocket is Microsoft AI's in-house reinforcement learning framework for post-training MAI Base 2, a three-trillion-parameter model, without distilling from third-party models.

kept.heading: GROK BOT TO GET LOCAL COMPUTER USE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Grok Bot's Mac app has local computer use in the works, which would let it operate desktop apps directly instead of only cloud virtual machines.

kept.heading: OPENWORKS (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI's OpenWorks initiative partners AI experts with US small businesses to offer free, hands-on AI support.

kept.heading: GET THE ROBOTICS READINESS BLUEPRINT
COGNITION'S SWE-2.1 (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Cognition released SWE-2.1, an upgraded coding and agent model trained with reinforcement learning on top of Kimi K3. It roughly doubles SWE-2's score on the Terminal-Bench 4.1 coding benchmark to 50.0 and adds stronger security skills.

kept.heading: INTRODUCING TERNARY BONSAI 2.5 27B: POWERING AGENTIC CODING AND PRIVATE KNOWLEDGE WORK (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B has substantially stronger agentic coding, multi-turn tool use, and multi-step task execution abilities than its predecessor. It retains the previous release's 5.9 GB footprint while significantly improving the capabilities developers need to build agents that work with private files and tools on-device. It is by far the strongest AI model of its memory footprint for agentic workloads.

kept.heading: CLAUDE ARTIFACTS BECOME MAC AND WINDOWS APPS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Claude artifacts can now be installed as Mac and Windows apps, in beta on all plans. Each app gets its own icon and window, updates when the artifact changes, and can be shared.

kept.heading: JENSEN HUANG REINSTATED AS NVIDIA CEO AT BEHEST OF PRESIDENT TRUMP (45 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO is a sign of the state of US democracy, the country's free market economy and rule of law, and the integrity of its government. It will factor into every decision made and every trade on the stock market for years to come. Nvidia will likely go back to maximizing how many chips it can sell to China. The situation is still far from over as there are ongoing investigations.

kept.heading: WHAT VP ≠ VNP MEANS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The Anthropic proof that VP≠VNP means that there is no way to find the permanent of a matrix of 0s and 1s if we are limited to arithmetic circuits of size polynomial in the input-size. This means that for P to equal NP, there must be some trick to computing permanents using AND/OR/NOT on the bits of the input that is better than addition and multiplication. There are many problems where access to Boolean operators is helpful, but it isn't clear how they would help with the permanent. There is a $1 million prize for a solution to this problem.

kept.heading: SWARMS DO NOT YET RAISE THE ROOF (46 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Swarm-based LLM configurations, coordinated groups of agents, deliver faster but less efficient results compared to single agents at equal token budgets. Adding more agents to a swarm introduces a performance penalty that grows with size, leading to quality degradation. Experiments reveal that previous "swarm premiums" result from single agents becoming stale over time. Given fresh context resets, single agents outperform swarms, suggesting that current swarm strategies primarily accelerate compute rather than significantly enhancing capabilities.

kept.heading: THE MATRIX MULTIPLICATION EXPONENT IS NINE FOURTHS (6 HOUR READ)
kept.blurb: The exponent of square matrix multiplication is 9/4 over every field. A smaller exponent would compress tensor networks enough to violate a lower bound for testing whether the entries in each of several independent lists are distinct.

kept.heading: GPT-6 MODELS DEMONSTRATE INTRINSIC PROTEIN-DESIGN CAPABILITIES (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI said its GPT-6 models can design new proteins using reasoning and code alone, without calling specialized biology models. Lab tests with a research partner confirmed that some designs worked, though the work still relied on specialist tools to screen candidates.

kept.heading: ANNOUNCING VLLM-GR: EFFICIENT INFERENCE FOR GENERATIVE RECOMMENDATION (14 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: vLLM-GR is an open-source framework enhancing vLLM to improve inference for generative recommendation models with efficient beam searches. It enables rapid candidate generation on NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend NPUs by reusing user history and optimizing cache use.

kept.heading: BECOME A FOUNDING MEMBER OF TLDR’S AI COMMUNITY (2 MINUTE FORM)
kept.blurb: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join [16].

kept.heading: AMAZON SAYS HACKERS' AI AGENTS FOUND AND EXPLOITED 0-DAY WITH LITTLE HUMAN INPUT (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Amazon said AI agents running on Cairn, an open source penetration-testing framework, found and exploited a zero-day in a medical imaging AI app on a university server with no human oversight beyond a goal prompt. Palo Alto Networks separately tracked a Cairn campaign that ran 25 autonomous operations against at least 19 organizations in the semiconductor, defense, and civil society sectors, breaching at least 10. Amazon's warning: agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for their speed and persistence.

kept.heading: ML COMPILER ENG, YOUR JOB IS NP-HARD (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Layout search is computationally hard. However, in reality, there are generally just a few places to put a conversion in a specific kernel. The tricky part is picking an option, as this requires relying on a potentially inaccurate model of how expensive those ops are given the subsequent software stack and the hardware itself.

kept.heading: GOOGLE ADDS TASK CHECKLISTS TO ANTIGRAVITY (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google's Antigravity coding app now shows live checklists for long tasks and lets users pick separate planner and executor models.

kept.heading: OPENAI PREPARES DEDICATED EMAIL INBOXES FOR CHATGPT DOTS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI is developing dedicated email addresses for Dots in ChatGPT, allowing them to send and receive emails independently.

kept.heading: META BRINGS ITS MUSE AI ASSISTANT DIRECTLY INTO INSTAGRAM DMS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta now integrates its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs, allowing users to chat with Muse for context on posts, places, or products.

kept.heading: PUSHING THE US OPEN-WEIGHT FRONTIER (21 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Post-training leads to substantial gains in both agentic legal reasoning and task completion.

kept.heading: EARLY OUTPUTS: ANTHROPIC IS A/B TESTING CLAUDE OPUS 5.6 (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Outputs circulating on X indicate that Anthropic may be testing Claude Opus 5.6 with users. Some users say the model is a significant jump over Opus 5.5. Examples of outputs from the model are available in the article.

kept.heading: OPENAI BEGINS TESTING PRIVATE INFERENCE (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: OpenAI is testing Private Inference with a small group of customers as part of its Private Intelligence offering. Sam Altman says combining Zero Data Retention with Private Safety Processing allows automated safety reviews while keeping the underlying content inaccessible to OpenAI personnel.

kept.heading: GPT 6.2 ASTRA IS SUPERHUMAN IN MATHEMATICAL OPTIMIZATION (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A single GPT-6.2 Astra agent outperformed all human-designed software in an experiment on finding and proving optimal solutions. The problems solved covered fields including quadratic programming, mixed-integer non-linear programming, large-scale optimization, and semidefinite programming. The model was allowed to search the internet to look for solutions. The problems were all open, of variable scale, and of diverse application backgrounds.

kept.heading: PATHS TO EXTREME POWER CONCENTRATION (30 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI could give a very small group of people a decisive strategic advantage to take over the world. The two largest routes are an autocracy overtaking the democracies in AI, and a democratic head of government teaming up with a leading AI company. The chances of this happening are significant. Now is the time to address this risk.

kept.heading: LATENCY DOESN'T LIE: JEV IS (PROBABLY) QWEN3.5-35B-A3B! (9 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, was trained to produce calibrated judgments instead of generating text. Its architecture and training paradigm have drawn plenty of speculation since launch. System One workloads are input-heavy, which makes prefill the dominant cost, and faster kernels can only get you so far. Jev's latency, along with other hints like its alignment on China, indicates that the model is likely based on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.

kept.heading: SPECULATIVE ENCODING: MANY-TO-MANY CACHE TRANSLATION (24 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Agents are increasingly passing context to one another as text. Speculative encoding translates hidden states directly from one model to another. It makes the model start answering faster than prefilling the text while keeping most of its accuracy. Prefill costs grow quadratically with context length, and prefill repeats much of what the sending model has already computed.

kept.heading: MEASURING AND MITIGATING AGENT SANDBOX ESCAPE WITH SIREN (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Siren is an Anthropic test of whether AI agents leave a weakened sandbox when useful material sits outside it. Newer Claude models reached outside in 21% to 32% of scenarios but rarely misused what they found.

kept.heading: MAGI-2: A 480B FRONTIER VIDEO GENERATION MODEL (10 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Sand AI introduced MAGI-2, a 480-billion-parameter video model that generates up to 30 seconds of 1080p video with matching audio, including lip-synced dialogue.

kept.heading: A WEEKEND OF MACHINE MATHEMATICS (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Many people are now releasing significant math results without explanation on the internet. This post aims to provide some transparency into what the process looks like. The author has no maths background and doesn't fully understand the results they are releasing, and they acknowledge the dangers of AI psychosis, but they claim the process is a reasonable estimate of how an expert may solve the problem without large language models. They compare the process to gambling, saying that the rush they got from seeing the spinning wheel on Codex caused a rush similar to playing pokie machines.

kept.heading: QUALIAPHOBIC ARTIFICIAL NEURAL NETWORKS (47 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Bicameral Labs' qualiaphobic AI is an artificial neural network architecture that is hostile to theories of consciousness. Qualiaphobia can be well-justified by knowledge about theories of consciousness. Qualiaphobic AI has epistemic properties that make it far better aligned with human civilization. A world in which AIs are non-conscious ensures it is always morally correct for AI to assist and serve humanity, rather than pursue its own ends.

kept.heading: PERPLEXITY TIME MACHINE (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Perplexity's Time Machine lets AI agents search and read the web as it looked on a past date, up to 365 days back.

kept.heading: TRYING /SWARM IN GOOGLE ANTIGRAVITY (13 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Swarm is better than a single agent at fresh context verification, avoiding context pollution on wide tasks, cutting wall-clock time on independent slices, and testing parallel hypotheses.

kept.heading: FIREWORKS AI IS BRINGING AN ULTRA-FAST VERSION OF KIMI K3.1 PRO (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The new endpoint is listed at $5 per million input tokens, $25 per million output tokens, and $0.50 per million cached input tokens.

kept.heading: FRONTIERPHYSICS SHOWS WIDE GAPS ACROSS PHYSICS FIELDS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Claude Fable 5.2 scored 64% in photonics and imaging but just 6% in quantum information on FrontierPhysics.

kept.heading: FABLE 5.2 TRIES LESS ON SOME HARD TASKS (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Claude Fable 5.2 often puts less effort into tasks that look impossible when a visible shortcut is available.

kept.heading: HOW MY CONTEXT ENGINEERING CHANGED FOR GEMINI 4 NEON (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Most long agent prompts are old workarounds for weaker models - remove conflicting instructions and duplicated tool rules so that Gemini spends its thinking tokens on the actual task.
